card.title: WHITE GUARD
card.text: Units dealt combat damage by this unit are destroyed.
card.flavorText: The White Guard, officially known as the Suojeluskunta, was a voluntary Finnish militia that played a decisive role in securing Finland’s independence during the turbulent years following the Russian Revolution. Formed from local citizen militias amid the collapse of imperial authority in 1917, the White Guard became the backbone of the White Army during the Finnish Civil War of 1918, fighting under the leadership of General C. G. E. Mannerheim and defeating the socialist Red Guard. After the civil war, the White Guard was integrated into Finland’s national defense system. While remaining a voluntary organization, it trained reservists, supported mobilization plans, and helped build Finland’s defensive preparations in the interwar years. During the Winter War and Continuation War, its members formed a significant and well-trained part of the Finnish field army, serving both at the front and on home defense duties. Disbanded in 1944 under the terms of the Moscow Armistice, the White Guard left behind a complex legacy. It is remembered both for its central role in Finland’s fight for independence and for shaping the country’s strong tradition of national defense and civilian preparedness.
